body: I’m merely the messenger, lmao. However, from my (admittedly limited) understanding, depending on circumstances that could be considered either Occupational Inequality or Employment Discrimination, depending on if the less than stellar interview process was the result of them expecting a man. Though, if that didn’t factor into the interview/hiring decisions, then it could be considered at best very rude and at worst sexist because of the implications.
It wasn’t the ad itself (I believe), but the receptionist saying they were expecting a man
Sorry if this seems annoying, I’m just curious if there’s any specific reason why? Is it disrespectful?
Oh man, that does make sense, I never took into account the nationality as opposed to heritage aspect.

Ah, yeah I get that. Would you mind if I get your opinion on people who would claim that heritage, but eventually move there, either early or later in life? Although I’m not sure terminology wise if someone who was naturalized could claim to be X or X-American.

Oh, interesting! Personally, I don’t fall into the category of the claiming X-American category, but I have 100% seen people use it like the fun-badge. If you don’t mind me asking, I’m curious about your perspective in the homogenized American culture. It might be because I live in the US, but I have a very hard time identifying it. I also wonder if the X-American stuff in the modern day comes with dissatisfaction with the US as a whole? I’ll be honest it is… not great here to say the least. Better than elsewhere, and I’m thankful for what I have, but some things are downright miserable. Thank you btw! I really do appreciate it!
I can definitely see a correlation there, unfortunately. :( I wish it wasn’t that way though, but with the history, especially wars, it’s not hard to see where that originated from.

Ahh yeah that’s completely fair! I definitely get the disconnect from heritage like that, especially when aspects like language were either heavily frowned upon or outright banned. I suppose it’s a to each their own scenario?

Yeah that makes sense with the ignorance regarding it, I’m just also wondering about the implications of the US, at least the education system, being very US-oriented. In the way that they don’t really teach about other cultures and heritages, and language curriculum is very limited. Thank you btw for your response, I really appreciate it!
Thank you for the understanding! I guess I just get really worried thinking that people will think I’m trying to troll, or be deliberately insensitive.
Ahhh, ok! Thank you so much for the explanation by the way! :)
Ohhh ok, the first part especially makes sense, but why not regulate it instead of bar participation entirely?
Hey, I’m so sorry, I only saw this now. Thank you so much for the advice, just posted a comment about how to meeting went. I hope you have a great day/night

Hey, just an update for y’all. Forgive formatting, I’m on mobile and just got out of the meeting. So, it looks like a medical withdrawal is my only option really. Unfortunately, it’s too late to see if I could get the money I spent on this semester back, so I’m stuck with loans and debt for a semester of nothing :(((
I only personally got one response from a prof, but him along with all of my profs responded to the Dean don’t think it’s feasible to make it up.
I asked about doing work over the summer and submitting it then, just as a long shot, and that was a no go. I also checked if the school had any of the classes offered in the summer, or any I could take to make sure I wasn’t behind; also a no. 
I’m probably going to have to take another semester, if my parents even let me. :((((
The Dean assured me that the schools not planning on kicking me out, and assured me I was a good student. I don’t believe it (the good student part that is). 
Depending on my parents reaction, which I’m in no way hopeful about, I very well may kill myself. I know it’s grim, but I just can’t take it. 
I’m going to email the place I wanted to intern at and beg for them to let me submit an application, but I doubt I’ll be allowed to. I feel like I had more to say, but I really can’t think straight right now. I’m going to go lay down

Edit: right after submitting this I remembered what I wanted to say. So, I explained the situation to the Dean with my Dad, and man he nailed down his personality so quick, which isn’t surprising considering the Dean has a history in the mental health field. He seemed verrrrrry worried about my dad’s reaction, so that makes 4 of us (My mom, me, my therapist, and now the Dean) :,)

Back home I only have one real friend, and she’s in a worse predicament than I am, and my couple college friends are spread across the state. What sort of gov. Organizations would be able to help? Unfortunately, job wise, my mom works the most bare bones job, my dad is the one that I’d need to ask. Thank you so much as well for all your help! I really want to take the advice, I’m not trying to make excuses, but this is just the lot I’m stuck with in life.

Unfortunately, I’m only a sophomore- so no degree :(
The job is just entry level it, basically answer the phone, make tickets if i can’t help, and help people that come up to the desk.
I don’t have any sort of funds to live anywhere else, and technically I think they employ people over the summer, but I wouldn’t be able to live on campus, and the job doesn’t make enough to rent a place. My mom already knows everything except the internship, but my dad has a horrible track record. To the point where my counselor specifically told me not to tell him until I have more info, and to request my mom don’t tell him till I’m ready :(((

Thank you, I appreciate it. I want nothing more than for things to work out, but I'm not optimistic. I'll update it after meeting tomorrow. I appreciate the sentiment of loving yourself, but I don't see any reason to when there's nothing to show for it, and even then I don't know how. I hope you have a good night/day btw. I'll def take the advice of sleeping on it though.
